questions.stem: An AM transmitter produces a modulated carrier whose envelope reaches a maximum of 12 V and a minimum of 4 V. Using the standard AM signal form x_AM(t) = A_c'[1 + a·m_n(t)]cos(2πf_c t), where m_n(t) is a normalized sinusoidal message (peak value ±1), determine the modulation index a.
questions.explanation:
The AM envelope peaks when m_n(t) = +1 and bottoms out when m_n(t) = -1, so:
V_max = A_c'(1 + a) = 12 V
V_min = A_c'(1 - a) = 4 V

Adding the two equations: 2A_c' = 16 → A_c' = 8 V.
Subtracting the two equations: 2A_c'·a = 8 → a = 8 / (2 × 8) = 0.5.

Check: A_c'(1+a) = 8(1.5) = 12 V ✓ and A_c'(1-a) = 8(0.5) = 4 V ✓. So the modulation index a = 0.50.
questions.reference: NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.6, Electrical and Computer Engineering — 'Amplitude Modulation (AM),' p.380

questions.stem: A communications engineer needs to send four independent voice signals simultaneously over a single shared channel by assigning each signal its own dedicated, non-overlapping carrier frequency band (rather than dividing the channel into time slots). Which multiplexing technique is being used?
questions.explanation:
Multiplexing techniques share a single physical channel among multiple signals by dividing a system resource:
- Time Division Multiplexing (TDM) divides the channel into sequential time slots, giving each signal the full channel bandwidth for a short time.
- Frequency Division Multiplexing (FDM) divides the channel's total bandwidth into separate, non-overlapping frequency sub-bands, one per signal, so all signals transmit simultaneously and continuously.
- Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) lets every signal share both the same time and frequency resources but distinguishes them using orthogonal spreading codes.
- PCM is a source-encoding/digitization method (sampling + quantizing), not a multiplexing scheme.

Since each signal gets its own dedicated frequency band for simultaneous transmission, this is FDM.
questions.reference: NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.6, Electrical and Computer Engineering — 'Communication Theory and Concepts,' p.377 (foundational concepts underlying the NCEES FE Multiplexing subtopic: TDM, FDM, CDMA)

questions.stem: A communication channel has a bandwidth of 3 kHz and a signal-to-noise power ratio (S/N) of 1023. Using the Shannon channel capacity formula, determine the maximum theoretical channel capacity.
questions.explanation:
The Shannon channel capacity formula is:
C = BW·log2(1 + S/N)

Substitute BW = 3000 Hz and S/N = 1023:
C = 3000 × log2(1 + 1023) = 3000 × log2(1024)

Since 2^10 = 1024, log2(1024) = 10 exactly.

C = 3000 × 10 = 30,000 bps = 30 kbps.
questions.reference: NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.6, Electrical and Computer Engineering — 'Shannon Channel Capacity Formula,' p.384

questions.stem: A periodic signal x(t) is represented by a complex-exponential Fourier series with nonzero coefficients X0 = 2, X1 = X-1 with |X1| = 1.5, and X2 = X-2 with |X2| = 1 (all other harmonics are zero). Using Parseval's theorem for Fourier series, determine the total average power in x(t).
questions.explanation:
Parseval's theorem for Fourier series gives the total average power as the sum over all harmonics:
P = Σ (n=-∞ to +∞) |Xn|^2 = X0^2 + 2·Σ(n=1 to N) |Xn|^2

Here N = 2 (harmonics beyond n=2 are zero):
P = (2)^2 + 2[(1.5)^2 + (1)^2]
P = 4 + 2[2.25 + 1]
P = 4 + 2(3.25)
P = 4 + 6.5 = 10.5 W

(Note: omitting the factor of 2 that accounts for both positive and negative harmonics — a common error — would incorrectly give 4 + 3.25 = 7.25 W, choice B.)
questions.reference: NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.6, Electrical and Computer Engineering — 'Parseval's Theorem for Fourier Series,' p.378

questions.stem: A voice signal is bandlimited to W = 4 kHz. It is sampled at the Nyquist rate and each sample is encoded as an n = 8-bit binary word (256 quantization levels) for pulse-code modulation (PCM) transmission. Determine the minimum number of binary pulses (bits) per second required to transmit this PCM signal.
questions.explanation:
For an n-bit PCM word length encoding a message bandlimited to W, transmission requires at least 2nW binary pulses per second (this also equals 2W·log2(q), since q = 2^n).

Given n = 8 bits and W = 4000 Hz:
Minimum bit rate = 2nW = 2 × 8 × 4000 = 64,000 bits/second (64 kbps).

(This matches the classic 64 kbps PCM voice channel used in digital telephony: an 8 kHz sample rate — satisfying the Nyquist criterion fs > 2W = 8000 Hz — times 8 bits/sample = 64,000 bps.) Choice A (32,000) omits the factor of 2 from the Nyquist/pulse-rate relationship; choices C and D are 2× and 4× the correct value.
questions.reference: NCEES FE Reference Handbook 10.6, Electrical and Computer Engineering — 'Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM),' p.382

items.text: In amplitude modulation, the modulation index a is found from the envelope's maximum and minimum voltages using a equals Vmax minus Vmin divided by Vmax plus Vmin.
items.source: FE Reference Handbook 10.6 — Amplitude Modulation (AM), p.380

items.text: Frequency division multiplexing separates multiple signals by assigning each one a unique carrier frequency band, letting them share a channel simultaneously instead of taking turns in time.
items.source: FE Reference Handbook 10.6 — Communication Theory and Concepts, p.377

items.text: The Shannon channel capacity formula states that the maximum data rate of a communication channel equals its bandwidth multiplied by the log base two of one plus the signal to noise ratio.
items.source: FE Reference Handbook 10.6 — Shannon Channel Capacity Formula, p.384

items.text: Parseval's theorem for Fourier series states that the total average power in a periodic signal equals the sum of the squared magnitudes of all its Fourier series coefficients.
items.source: FE Reference Handbook 10.6 — Parseval's Theorem for Fourier Series, p.378

items.text: In pulse code modulation, transmitting an n-bit encoded message bandlimited to W hertz requires a minimum bit rate of two times n times W binary pulses per second.
items.source: FE Reference Handbook 10.6 — Pulse-Code Modulation (PCM), p.382
